a b s t r a c t
The traditional distributed flexible job shop scheduling problem (DFJSP) assumes that operations of a job
cannot be transferred between different factories. However, in real-world production settings, the oper-
ations of a job may need to be processed in different factories owing to requirements of economic glob-
alization or complexity of the job. Hence, in this paper, we propose a distributed flexible job shop
scheduling problem with transfers (DFJSPT), in which operations of a job can be processed in different
factories. An efficient memetic algorithm (EMA) is proposed to solve the DFJSPT with the objectives of
minimizing the makespan, maximum workload, and total energy consumption of factories. In the pro-
posed EMA, a well-designed chromosome presentation and initialization methods are presented to obtain
a high-quality initial population. Several crossover and mutation operators and three effective neighbor-
hood structures are designed to expand the search space and accelerate the convergence speed of the
solution. Forty benchmark instances of the DFJSPT are constructed to evaluate the EMA and facilitate fur-
ther studies. The Taguchi method of design of experiments is used to obtain the best combination of key
EMA parameters. Extensive computational experiments are carried out to compare the EMA with three
well-known algorithms from the literature. The computational results show that the EMA can obtain bet-
ter solutions for approximately 90% of the tested benchmark instances compared to the three well
known algorithms, thereby demonstrating the DFJSPT’s competitive performance and efficiency.

From the above, we can make the following observations: all
the studies on the DFJSPs assumed that the jobs could not be trans-
ferred among different factories, i.e., operations of a job must be
processed in the same factory; however, in real-world production
systems, certain jobs may have to be processed in different facto-
ries because of reasons, such as complexity of operations or eco-
nomic globalization. In addition, under energy-saving era, most
of researchers focused on single objective (makespan) in DFJSP,
which led to the production managers focused on economic indica-
tor but ignored other important factors, such as energy consump-
tion generated by processing and transferring jobs.
Inspired by these findings, in this study, we propose a dis-
tributed flexible job shop scheduling problem with transfers
(DFJSPT), in which the jobs can be transferred among factories.
The memetic algorithms (MAs), which hybridize evolutionary algo-
rithms with local search (Burdett & Kozan, 2014; Chiong, Weise, &
Michalewicz, 2012; Gong, et al., 2019; Kannan & Ramaraj, 2010),
have delivered promising performance for solving multi-objective
FJSPs (Frutos, Olivera, & Tohmé, 2010; Gong, Deng, Gong, Liu, &
Ren, 2018; Wenchao, Xinyu, & Baolin, 2016; Yuan & Xu, 2013;
Yuan & Xu, 2015). Motivated by their work and based on the fact
that it’s hard or even impossible to obtain the optimal solutions
in the acceptable time for the NP-hard problems (eg., FJSP (Gong,
et al., 2020), DFJSP (De Giovanni & Pezzella, 2010), and our DFJSPT)
by using mixed integer programming approaches, we present an
effective memetic algorithm (EMA) to solve our proposed DFJSPT
with the objectives of minimizing the makespan, maximum work-
load of factories, and total energy consumption. In the EMA, an
effective initialization method that combines global, local, and ran-
dom selections, and a crossover operator are used to obtain a high-
quality initial population and improve the solution diversity. In
addition, a well-designed local search operator (LSO) is proposed
and integrated into the EMA to improve its convergence speed
and fully exploit its solution space. In addition, 40 benchmark
instances are constructed to test the EMA’s performance and facil-
itate our future study. Finally, a suitable combination of key
parameters in the EMA, which includes population size (POP_size),
crossover rate (CR_rate), mutation rate (MU_rate), and local search
rate (LS_rate) is obtained by using the Taguchi method of Design of
Experiments (DOE) (Montgomery, 2008). Extensive experiments
carried out on these 40 instances confirm the superior performance
of the EMA compared to the non-dominated sorting genetic algo-
rithm II (NSGA-II) (Deb, Pratap, Agarwal, & Meyarivan, 2002),
non-dominated neighbor immune algorithm (NNIA) (Gong, Jiao,
Du, & Bo, 2008) and non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm III
(NSGA-III) (Deb & Jain, 2014).
The rest of this paper is organized as follows. In Section 2, a
mathematical model of the DFJSPT is presented. In Section 3, the
EMA is described in detail. The numerical experiments and
discussions are presented in Section 4. Finally, we draw some con-
clusions and describe the future work in Section 5.

3.2.6. Local search operator (LSO)
In this section, an LSO is proposed to accelerate the convergence
speed and expand the solution space of the EMA. Many previous
studies, such as Yuan and Xu (2015) and Wang, Zhou, Xu, Wang,
and Liu (2012), demonstrated that the makespan for a predeter-
mined scheduling could be minimized only by moving the opera-
tions on the critical path (also called the critical operations path).
Hence, taking inspiration from the aforementioned studies, here,
we design three methods for the LSO. The first method swaps
two positions of the critical operations (LSO_SP) based on critical
blocks (Li, Pan, & Liang, 2010). The second method converts the
current factory and machine to other alternatives with a minimum
processing time (LSO_MPT). The third method replaces the current
factory and machine with other alternatives that can reduce the
transfer time to the maximum extent possible (LSO_RTT). The core
pseudo code of the LSO is shown in Algorithm 2, while two other
pseudo codes related to the three LSOs are given in Algorithms 3
and 4 respectively.

5. Conclusions and future studies
In this study, we proposed an extended model of distributed
flexible job shop scheduling problem (DFJSP), i.e. distributed flexi-
ble job shop scheduling problem with transfers (DFJSPT), in which
jobs can be processed in multiple factories by transfers. A mathe-
matical model of DFJSPT was constructed with the optimization
objectives of makespan, maximum workload of the factories, and
the total energy consumption simultaneously. An effective meme-
tic algorithm (EMA) was developed to solve this model. The effec-
tiveness of the EMA has been proved by a variety of experiments,
and the computational results can provide the best or near best
solutions with three objectives for distributed factory managers
from a global perspective.
The proposed model of DFJSPT makes full use of distributed
resources in many factories to obtain the overall optimal produc-
tion solution. In this model, each job has several operations, and
these operations can be processed in many factories. To the best
of our knowledge, the traditional researches normally assume that
all operations of the same job can only be processed in a factory.
However, in the real production, the operations of a job may need
to be processed in different factories, or more optimal scheduling
solutions can be obtained if the operations of jobs can be processed
in different factories considering the production resource compre-
hensively. Hence. We extended the existing model of DFJSP, in
which each operation could be assigned to an appropriate machine
in the distributed factories. Besides, under the context of globaliza-
tion and saving energy, more indicators should be taken into
account in the scheduling model, such as energy consumption,
but the previous papers normally focused on single objective
(makespan) in their model, which may consume excessive
resources to complete the economic objective, and ultimately lead
to waste of energy. With regards to this, we formed a multi-
objective optimization model, where the makespan, workload of
factories, and energy consumption were considered simultane-
ously. This twofold improvements of the proposed model can pro-
vide a reference for the subsequent research on DFJSP.
We proposed an EMA to solve the DFJSPT aiming at optimizing
the makespan, workload of factories, and energy consumption
simultaneously. In the EMA, a well-designed three levels encoding
method, and some crossover and mutation operators were inte-
grated. A specially designed GLR initialization method, which
includes global (G), local (L), and random (R) selection methods,
was used to obtain a high-quality initial population, and three
neighborhood structures based on the critical path in the local
search operator (LSO) were proposed to improve the convergence
speed and fully exploit the solution space. In our experiments, a
total of 40 benchmark instances of the DFJSPT were first constructed
to facilitate the verification of the performance of the EMA. Next, we
used the Taguchi method of DOE to obtain the best combination of
key parameters in the EMA. Finally, extensive comparisons were
carried out between our proposed EMA and three well-known algo-
rithms based on the constructed benchmarks. From the comparison
results, we see that the EMA outperforms other three compared
algorithms more than about 90% of the tested benchmarks.
Owing to requirements of globalization, this research provided
theoretical and practical significance. Theoretically, we have devel-
oped a research direction for the DFJSP and proposed an effective
algorithm to solve the problem. From a practical stand point, our
constructed DFJSPT model can support production managers who
work in distributed manufacturing units in scheduling jobs in a
manner that is in line with the actual production. If production
managers could consider job transfers among distributed factories,
they can produce a more feasible and efficient scheduling scheme.
As part of a future work, we plan to study the DFJSPT in more
detail. For example, we shall consider the dynamic transfer time
between machines, and the batch transportation of jobs between
factories in distributed flexible job shop scheduling problem.
